gen_risks.description: Financial management deficiencies such as delays in transaction recording, reporting, or internal audits may weaken financial controls and implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Designate an experienced project accountant, customize the computerized accounting software, and incorporate clear criteria in the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: FM risks identified include: (i) delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports; (ii) internal audit reviews not conducted

gen_risks.description: Marginalized groups in remote regions or low-income households risk exclusion or elite capture in the selection of sub-grant and training beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target beneficiaries using the Unique Social Registry (USR), apply strict female participation quotas, and establish transparent selection criteria in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: risks of exclusion, which may arise if project benefits are not equitably distributed... as well as risks of elite capture in the selection of beneficiaries

gen_risks.description: Female beneficiaries participating in technical training or internship placements face risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and sexual harassment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire a Social Specialist with GBV/SEA/SH expertise, implement safe training guidelines, and enforce SEA/SH prevention mechanisms in provider contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: community health and safety risks, including risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH), particularly for young women

gen_risks.description: Minor civil works and small business activities in agriculture, fisheries, or tourism may generate waste or cause localized pressure on sensitive island ecosystems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint an Environmental Specialist, conduct environmental screening for sub-grants, and enforce EDGE design standards and construction waste management.
gen_risks.evidence: small business grants could support micro-enterprises in agriculture, fisheries, or tourism that may indirectly place pressure on sensitive ecosystems or cause localized pollution

gen_risks.description: Delays or weak collaboration between MLSSS and AFAP in providing technical inputs and terms of reference could stall key procurement processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish standard operational workflows in the POM and maintain close operational oversight through a unified PIU and Ministerial Coordination Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: A key factor for good procurement performance will be the ability of AFAP and the MLSSS to work in close collaboration

gen_risks.description: Failure to recruit key PIU and AFAP specialists within contractual deadlines after effectiveness may cause operational and compliance delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate recruitment and terms of reference preparation early, prioritizing the hiring of environmental, social, TVET, and IT specialists.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall cause AFAP to hire or appoint, not later than forty-five (45) days after Effectiveness: (i) one Environmental Specialist...

gen_risks.description: Recurrent climate events such as severe storms, flash flooding, and rising sea levels may disrupt project service delivery and cause operational delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient designs for new infrastructure, install back-up generators and cloud systems for digital tools, and phase training delivery.
gen_risks.evidence: Key climate and disaster risks that may affect the project include floods, droughts, and rising sea levels... cause disruptions in service delivery

gen_risks.description: Extreme geographic isolation and insularity of Príncipe island increase logistics complexity and costs for constructing the new technical training center.
gen_risks.mitigation: Refine cost assumptions through detailed architectural and engineering studies, utilize local materials, and manage contingencies through the procurement plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Príncipe—home to just about 10,000 people—is more than 170 km away and experiences compounded isolation.

gen_risks.description: Target public TVET centers possess outdated equipment, staffing gaps, and weak employer links, threatening the market relevance of technical training.
gen_risks.mitigation: Form Workforce Development Committees with private employers, modernize equipment, and tie institutional co-financing to training performance in priority skills.
gen_risks.evidence: capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps, and weak employer participation

gen_risks.description: Failure or delay in contracting an eligible payment agent satisfies a disbursement condition that would block stipend, grant, and scholarship payouts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize the early competitive procurement of a qualified electronic Payment Service Provider (PSP) following established social protection models.
gen_risks.evidence: For Disbursement category 2 'Sub-Grants': The Recipient has (i) hired a payment agent in accordance with Section I.F of Schedule 2

gen_risks.description: The new LMIS and Employability Portal risk low operational uptake or abandonment, repeating failures of earlier tools like the ILO Employment Observatory.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early user mapping, engage specialized IT consultancies, mandate portal usage for program participants, and incentivize private employer listings.
gen_risks.evidence: Employment Observatory was previously developed with support from the International Labour Organization (ILO) but never fully operationalized

gen_risks.description: High dependence on ODA and volatile domestic revenues expose the government to macroeconomic shocks that could jeopardize institutional sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed job programs within line ministry operations, leverage private sector demand in growth sectors, and foster co-financing with international partners.
gen_risks.evidence: Persistently low domestic revenue mobilization has kept STP heavily dependent on Official Development Assistance (ODA)... leaving fiscal revenues highly volatile.

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
